title: Twenty Seconds, Five Steps
bigQuestion: How do you know your hands are really clean?

story.title: How Long Is Twenty Seconds?
story.kicker: The class has no clock at the sink, so they find another way to count.
paragraphs: Ms. Bell asked the class to wash for twenty seconds. Diego turned on the water. He rubbed his hands. He counted, "one, two, three, four, five, done!" It took about three seconds. His hands still had marker on them.

"We need a way to count," said Ms. Bell. "There is no clock at the sink." Priya had an idea. "We could sing!" The class tried the birthday song. They sang it once. Ms. Bell watched the clock. "Ten seconds," she said.
"So sing it twice," said Diego. They tried again. Wet, soap, scrub. They sang the birthday song two times. Ms. Bell called out, "Twenty seconds!" Diego looked at his hands. The marker was gone.
From then on, the sink had a song. Anyone walking past the bathroom could hear it. Two rounds. Twenty seconds. Clean hands, every time.
story.think: What song could you sing two times to count twenty seconds?

lessons.title: Wet and Lather
lessons.mainIdea: Step one is wet your hands, and step two is lather with soap.
reading: Stand at the sink. Turn on the water. Warm or cold both work. Step one: *wet* your hands all over. Both sides. Then turn the water off to save water.
Step two: get soap. One pump or one rub of the bar is enough. Rub your hands together. Rub until you see bubbles. The bubbles are called *lather*. Lather means the soap is working.
Wet first, then soap. If you put soap on dry hands, it will not spread. No bubbles means no lather.

words.d: the bubbles you make when you rub soap with water

look.title: The Dry-Hand Mistake
look.text: Picture Ali at the sink. He grabs soap first. He rubs it on his dry hands. It sticks in one spot and will not spread. He rubs harder. Still no bubbles.
look.prompt: What step did Ali skip? What should he do to fix it?

check.q: What is step one of washing hands?
check.why: Wet hands first so the soap can spread and make lather.

check.q: What are the bubbles called?
check.why: Lather is the bubbles made by rubbing soap with water.

check.q: Ali put soap on dry hands. What went wrong?
check.why: Soap needs water to spread and make lather, so wet first.

lessons.title: Scrub Every Part
lessons.mainIdea: Step three is scrub for twenty seconds: backs, between fingers and under nails.
reading: Step three: *scrub*. This is the big one. Rub your palms together. Now rub the backs of your hands. Germs hide there too.
Lace your fingers together. Rub between them. Rub around your thumbs. Now scratch your nails on your palm. Germs love to hide under nails.
Scrub for twenty seconds. That is longer than it feels. Most people stop too soon. Keep going.

words.d: to rub hard all over to get something clean
the flat inside part of your hand

look.title: Spots People Forget
look.cite: the four scrub spots, in order
look.prompt: Which spot is easiest to forget? Point to it on your own hand.

check.q: Where do germs like to hide?
check.why: Nails trap dirt and germs, so scratch them on your palm while scrubbing.

check.q: How long should you scrub?
check.why: Twenty seconds of scrubbing is the standard time to get hands clean.

check.q: Which part do people often skip?
check.why: People rub palms and forget the backs of the hands and between fingers.

lessons.title: Rinse and Dry
lessons.mainIdea: Step four is rinse under running water, and step five is dry with a clean towel.
reading: Step four: rinse. Turn the water back on. Hold your hands under it. Let the water carry the soap and germs away. Rinse until no bubbles are left.
Step five: dry. Wet hands pick up germs faster than dry ones. Use a clean paper towel. Or use the air dryer. Dry all over.
Then use the towel to turn off the tap. Now your clean hands never touch the dirty handle.

words.d: the handle you turn to start or stop the water

look.title: Order the Steps
look.text: Here are the five steps, but they are mixed up: dry, wet, rinse, lather, scrub. Say them out loud in the right order. Then act them out with pretend water.
look.prompt: What is the right order? What happens if you rinse before you scrub?

check.q: What is the last step?
check.why: Drying is step five; wet hands pick up germs faster than dry ones.

check.q: Why use the towel on the tap?
choices: So clean hands do not touch the dirty handle
check.why: The handle was touched by dirty hands, so the towel keeps your clean hands clean.

check.q: What is the right order of the five steps?
check.why: Wet, lather, scrub, rinse, dry is the standard order.

lessons.title: Sing It Twice
lessons.mainIdea: Twenty seconds is about two rounds of a short song like the birthday song.
reading: Twenty seconds is longer than it feels. Counting fast does not work. A song works better. The birthday song takes about ten seconds. Sing it two times. That is about twenty seconds.
Sing it in your head or out loud. Scrub the whole time. Do not stop when the first song ends. Start it again.
Try other songs too. Pick a short one. Sing it twice. Ask a grown-up to time you once.

words.d: a very short bit of time; a slow count of one is about one second

look.title: One Song or Two?
look.text: Picture Mara at the sink. She sings the birthday song one time while she scrubs. She stops. She rinses. Beside her, Jun sings it two times before rinsing.
look.prompt: Who scrubbed for about twenty seconds? How many seconds did the other one get?

check.q: How many times do you sing the birthday song?
check.why: One round is about ten seconds, so two rounds make about twenty.

check.q: Mara sang it once and stopped. About how long did she scrub?
check.why: One round of the song is about ten seconds, only half the time needed.

check.q: Why not just count fast to twenty?
choices: Fast counting is much shorter than twenty seconds
check.why: Counting fast takes only a few seconds; a song keeps a steady pace.

lessons.title: A Clean Towel
lessons.mainIdea: Dry your hands on something clean, or the germs come right back.
reading: Your hands are clean. Now do not put germs back on them. A dirty towel has germs. Your shirt has germs. A clean paper towel does not.
At school, take one paper towel. Dry your hands. Throw it in the trash. At home, use a clean cloth towel. Ask a grown-up to change it often.
An air dryer works too. Hold your hands under it until they are all the way dry. Wet hands pick up germs.

look.title: Three Ways to Dry
look.text: Picture three kids. Ana wipes her wet hands on her jeans. Cole uses the same cloth towel that has hung by the sink all week. Ivy takes one clean paper towel.
look.prompt: Whose hands stay clean? What is wrong with the other two ways?

check.q: What should you dry your hands with?
check.why: A clean towel keeps germs from going back onto washed hands.

check.q: Ana wiped her hands on her jeans. What happened?
choices: Germs from the jeans got on her hands
check.why: Clothes carry germs, so drying on them undoes the washing.

check.q: What goes wrong with a towel used all week?
check.why: A towel used for days collects germs; a clean one should replace it often.

lessons.title: Hand Sanitizer Helps
lessons.mainIdea: Hand sanitizer is a backup when there is no sink, but soap and water are better.
reading: You are on a field trip. No sink. It is snack time. What now? Use *hand sanitizer*. Squirt a small amount in your palm. Rub it all over both hands. Keep rubbing until they feel dry.
Sanitizer kills many germs. But it does not lift dirt. If your hands look dirty, it will not work well. Soap and water are always better.
Sanitizer is not for eating or for playing. It is only for hands. Ask a grown-up to help you use it.

words.d: a gel you rub on your hands to kill germs when there is no sink

look.title: Sink or Squirt?
look.text: Picture two places. One: the school lunchroom, with a sink right by the door. Two: a picnic table at the park, with no sink anywhere near. Both times it is snack time and your hands are dirty from playing.
look.prompt: Which place is right for sanitizer? Which place should use soap and water?

check.q: When is hand sanitizer a good choice?
choices: When you have soap and water
check.why: Sanitizer is a backup for times with no sink; soap and water are better.

check.q: Your hands are covered in mud. What works best?
check.why: Sanitizer does not lift dirt; soap and water wash it away.

check.q: How do you use sanitizer?
choices: Rub it all over until dry
check.why: Rub sanitizer over both hands until they feel dry, with a grown-up's help.

lessons.title: Brush Twice a Day
lessons.mainIdea: Brush your teeth two times a day, morning and night, for two minutes.
reading: Germs live in your mouth too. They eat bits of food stuck on your teeth. That can make holes in teeth. Brushing sweeps the germs and food away.
Brush in the morning. Brush before bed. Use a pea-sized bit of toothpaste. Brush the front, the back and the tops of your teeth. Brush for two minutes. Sing a song here too.
Rinse your brush. Stand it up to dry. Get a new brush when the bristles bend out.

words.d: a small brush with bristles for cleaning teeth
the short stiff hairs on a brush

look.title: Clean Habits Each Day
look.cite: example day and year for one student
look.prompt: How many times a day is brushing? Which habit happens most often in a day?

check.q: How many times a day should you brush?
check.why: Brush in the morning and before bed, two times a day.

check.q: How much toothpaste do you use?
check.why: A pea-sized bit is enough for a child's brush.

check.q: When do you get a new toothbrush?
check.why: Bent bristles do not clean well, so the brush gets replaced.

review.q: What is the first of the five steps?
review.why: Wet hands first so soap can spread; the order is wet, lather, scrub, rinse, dry.

review.q: How long is the scrub step?
review.why: Twenty seconds is the standard scrub time, about two rounds of a short song.

review.q: Which spot do people forget to scrub?
review.why: Germs hide under nails, so scratch them on your palm while you scrub.

review.q: You are at the park with no sink. What can you use?
review.why: Sanitizer is the backup when there is no sink, rubbed in until dry.

review.q: Why is a clean towel important?
choices: A dirty towel puts germs back on clean hands
review.why: Drying on something dirty undoes the washing.

review.q: How long should you brush your teeth?
review.why: Brushing takes two minutes, two times a day.
